learning_outcomes.text: Students know the problems that arise when calculating with floating-point numbers and have learned methods to examine algorithms for their stability.
Students know a number of different numerical methods for relevant application problems and can select the appropriate one based on the properties of the methods.
Students have gained initial experience with the practical implementation of numerical algorithms in computer programs.
Students are able to work independently and in teams, depending on the question, and to apply their knowledge of mathematics to new problems.
They can partially solve emerging problems independently with the help of literature.
In the event of greater difficulties, students can specifically seek help.
Students work persistently even on more complex problems.

syllabus_topics: Floating-point numbers, rounding errors and stability
Solution of linear equation systems: Conditioning, LR decomposition, Pivoting, Irregular systems
Iterative solution of linear and non-linear equation systems
teaching_methods: Demonstrations and exercises on the computer

assessment_methods.method: Successful completion of exercise tasks in homework and/or in-class exercises

assessment_rules: If there are 10 or more participants, the assessment is a written exam (120 minutes). If there are fewer than 10 participants, the assessment is an oral exam (30 minutes, individual examination). Homework exercises are a mandatory prerequisite for the written/oral exam.
